title: Prove ordered centre interfaces and price two complete D25 terminal constructions
body:
This PR adds enabling proofs for ordered centre controllers, a conditional physical coordinate compiler, and an exact 224-role construction over the regular D25 cover. It also gives a scoped negative result: both stated paid terminal constructions fail the native moment test for every positive improvement exponent. **There is no improvement to the complete kappa calculation.**

The [proof](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/4258585b17450907d26b137c047e254cd9007bae/research/ordered-centre-interfaces/PROOF.md), [fresh replay receipt](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/4258585b17450907d26b137c047e254cd9007bae/research/ordered-centre-interfaces/validation/REPLAY.json), [independent publication review](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/4258585b17450907d26b137c047e254cd9007bae/research/publication-reviews/ordered-centre-interfaces/REVIEW.md), and [source pins](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/4258585b17450907d26b137c047e254cd9007bae/research/ordered-centre-interfaces/SOURCES.json) define the claim.

The raw and weighted controller normal forms hold for every positive pair count. The general-unit one-pair word gives `(-y,T x)`, where `T=E2 G1^-1 E0`. Its physical residual is `diag(Q T Q^-1,I)`. The multiplication order is part of the result. The theorem assumes the stated local responses and common-frame scalar access; a content inverse alone does not supply a native decoder or a retired-data view.

The physical compiler must change coordinates on the complete state, including helpers, and must keep every composed map inside the admitted grammar. Its line-flag result excludes the stated independent-path transfer; the finite canonical-prefix screen is not an exclusion of all stabilizer choices. A separate completion preserves 408 arbitrary helpers and their productive maps, with 2,326 children and rank mass 3,281. That completion is not an extra charge in the data-only D25 word.

The D25 construction has three calls of native rank mass 1,792 each. Either terminal adds **224**, so the complete mass is **5,600 = 224*25**. These are costs of two specified constructions, not a lower bound for all possible terminals.

| Terminal | Added terminal children | Complete native profile | Real scalar subtotal |
| --- | --- | --- | ---: |
| Separated | 224 rank-one children | `{1:704,2:144,5:144,7:336,8:192}` | 28,264 |
| Mixed | 96 rank-one and 64 rank-two children | `{1:576,2:208,5:144,7:336,8:192}` | 25,896 |

The mixed terminal saves 2,368 scalar primitives under the same scalar prices. Every child in both complete profiles has rank below 25, which proves the strict positive-moment failure. The scalar subtotals exclude the old signed exchange, global cover work, finite map prices, recursive storage, and precision. The mixed terminal has a separate count of 608 map calls; that count is not their finite operation price. A cheaper terminal remains possible.

The [common-cover terminal annex](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/4258585b17450907d26b137c047e254cd9007bae/research/ordered-centre-interfaces/annexes/common-cover-terminal/README.md) adds a distinct D=73 construction and a sharp standalone limit. For the actual common ten-cycle cover response, the raw controller gives (-E^-1 y,Ex) for every positive pair count. The ordered physical terminal returns (FQx,Fy) on arbitrary inputs without assuming E commutes with Q. Per four-pair replica, it uses **448 rank-two children, rank mass 896, and 1344 monomial maps**. It removes the old 448 line-square maps, so the net map increase is 896. The signed exchange retains its 10752 real primitives. These are component counts, separate from the existing paid D25 terminals.

For every admitted orthogonal extension L with Lq=v and q^T v=0, the standalone one-field Clifford terminal has rank at least two per X field. The actual recipe attains this bound. The [proof and original independent review](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/4258585b17450907d26b137c047e254cd9007bae/research/ordered-centre-interfaces/annexes/common-cover-terminal/frozen/lanes/independent-review-20261017/common-terminal-review-20261018/REVIEW.md) cover all such extensions; finite dimensions are controls, not the basis of the theorem. Field mixing, a changed first cut, a payload response, and fusion with earlier work are outside the class. The native-moment equality remains conditional on the complete path and idle ledger. **No complete kappa improvement follows.** Fresh local native emission, global scheduling, hosting, finite map price, and precision remain separate.

The [fresh receipt](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/4258585b17450907d26b137c047e254cd9007bae/research/ordered-centre-interfaces/annexes/common-cover-terminal/evidence/REPLAY.json) records the unchanged independent terminal checker and finite rank checker in normal and optimized Python. All four outputs match their frozen bytes. The checks bind all 112 ports, complete Z4 phase and affine Gaussian kernel coefficients, negative controls, and the dimension-three/five enumeration. The annex preserves all eighteen source files and leaves the accepted parent manifest unchanged. With Python 3.11+, the standard library, at least 3 GiB free, and a new output directory:

```sh
python3 -I -B research/ordered-centre-interfaces/annexes/common-cover-terminal/replay.py --out /tmp/common-cover-terminal-annex
```

Expected final line:

```text
PASS_COMMON_COVER_TERMINAL_ANNEX
```

The [annex notice](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/4258585b17450907d26b137c047e254cd9007bae/research/ordered-centre-interfaces/annexes/common-cover-terminal/NOTICE.md) credits the bridge-access, encoded-controller, and independent-review source lanes and retains the parent source lineage. The original source pins and Apache-2.0 terms stay fixed. Substantial OpenAI Codex assistance was used.

The [separate common-terminal review](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/4258585b17450907d26b137c047e254cd9007bae/research/publication-reviews/ordered-centre-interfaces/common-terminal-review/REVIEW.md) binds the exact annex and repeats its four checks from a relocated copy.

The [varying-response controller appendix](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/4258585b17450907d26b137c047e254cd9007bae/research/ordered-centre-interfaces/annexes/reciprocal-controller/PROOF.md) adds an independently reviewed all-pair construction for reciprocal routed responses. With `m` pairs, `4m+1` code factors at explicitly typed cuts restore the raw `(-y_i,x_i)` content endpoint and the retained physical terminal. A common routed response reduces this construction to `2m+2` factors. These counts are conditional code placements, not native costs. Exact reciprocal native words, future and past code access, restoration, and complete pricing remain required. The original free-word checker passes for one through eight pairs in normal Python and with `-O`.

```sh
python3 -I -B research/ordered-centre-interfaces/annexes/reciprocal-controller/replay.py --out /tmp/reciprocal-controller-replay
```

Expected final line:

```text
PASS_SCOPED_SUPPORT_PROOF_REPLAY
```

The [separate varying-response review](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/4258585b17450907d26b137c047e254cd9007bae/research/ordered-centre-interfaces/annexes/reciprocal-controller/REVIEW.md) checks the all-pair induction and typed factor placement. Its [manifest](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/4258585b17450907d26b137c047e254cd9007bae/research/ordered-centre-interfaces/annexes/reciprocal-controller/ANNEX-MANIFEST.json) binds the unchanged source closure. Both new reviews are independent agent reviews, not human peer reviews.

Run from the repository root with Python 3.11 or later, its standard library, at least 3 GiB free disk, and a new output directory:

```sh
python3 -I -B research/ordered-centre-interfaces/replay.py --out /tmp/ordered-centre-replay
```

Expected final output:

```text
PASS_ORDERED_CENTRE_INTERFACES
```

All ten checks passed normally and with optimized Python. The independent review repeated all 20 runs in a Git-free copy with no executable search path and verified all 128 source inputs. Its separate exact checker verifies ordered unit identities, complete-state coordinate changes, all four 224-column data words, both paid profiles, 2,688 small symplectic compositions, and seven negative controls. The all-size statements come from the proofs. One portable checker reads an exact retained archive member; only its changed self-hash is excluded from the old receipt comparison. The [adaptation record](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/4258585b17450907d26b137c047e254cd9007bae/research/ordered-centre-interfaces/PORTABLE-ADAPTATION.json) retains the original script and exact diff.

The raw native phase reviews, serial cover, row split, and LIFO contracts remain pinned premises. No full native phase sweep, selected-construction replay, all-size recursive compiler proof, finite map/tape invoice, precision proof, or exact integer-recovery proof was run.

The packaging base is [b58ad9ef4d4e861b0eaa5dba41742bdc072dca51](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/commit/b58ad9ef4d4e861b0eaa5dba41742bdc072dca51), which selects [PR #4470](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/4470). This PR makes no applicability claim for that selected construction. The historical pins remain unchanged.

The coupled provider comes from [PR #3133](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/3133) at [51eb9c4ee9e4722010d308aa3309e039d3940cc2](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/51eb9c4ee9e4722010d308aa3309e039d3940cc2/research/rank7-coupled-586-588-carrier-fold/README.md), whose source credits @dcharb78. The byte-equal provider copies come from Jeremy Diviney (@jeremydiviney) in [PR #3148](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/3148) at [f2927a4b8afcf0701a6b945e14f30de1d94f5176](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/f2927a4b8afcf0701a6b945e14f30de1d94f5176/research/coupled-carrier-cap740/README.md). The exact Clifford implementation comes from [PR #2588](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2588) at [8cd9dc88e24f062e2ca2fa7f4844a3d3319381fb](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/8cd9dc88e24f062e2ca2fa7f4844a3d3319381fb/research/gmx-t74-borrow43-handoff/new/code/borrow/vendor/clifford/clifford_exact.py). The [notice](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/4258585b17450907d26b137c047e254cd9007bae/research/ordered-centre-interfaces/NOTICE.md) preserves the full earlier credit and Apache-2.0 terms. Substantial OpenAI Codex assistance was used; the independent reviews are separate agent checks.

The [terminal rank annex](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/70b3c9ad0ee50502f91c31834ac7babc2ff52515/research/ordered-centre-interfaces/annexes/rank-completions/PROOF.md) preserves two completed results. The pure-cycle bound is 65,408 native rank units per cover copy for four pairs and 112 ports. It requires tensor width at least three, independent productive inputs at every owner, and one common basis on each fixed-port ten-owner orbit. Each native call uses a coordinate subset of that basis and pays at least its size. Complete children are atomic, and free translations act uniformly on the tensor copies. The bound does not cover general cross-port mixing. The rank-nine contraction replaces 64 rank-seven completions and 64 rank-two terminal children with 64 rank-nine children, for both providers. It removes 64 children and leaves rank mass at 5,600. The target has a sharp native rank bound of nine in the stated one-field Clifford class with monomial wrappers. This excludes cross-field scalar mixing and changed targets.

The [source pins](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/70b3c9ad0ee50502f91c31834ac7babc2ff52515/research/ordered-centre-interfaces/annexes/rank-completions/SOURCES.json), [credit and license](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/70b3c9ad0ee50502f91c31834ac7babc2ff52515/research/ordered-centre-interfaces/annexes/rank-completions/NOTICE.md), and [separate review](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/70b3c9ad0ee50502f91c31834ac7babc2ff52515/research/publication-reviews/ordered-centre-interfaces/rank-completions-review/REVIEW.md) preserve the exact source records. The portable replay runs both unchanged independent checkers in normal and optimized Python. It checks all 336 fresh native recipes, all 64 contractions per provider, complete global phases, chronology, and the invoice. The negative controls reject an added global phase, a non-coordinate native line under the coordinate-subset test, a single-copy translation, and wrong rank-nine signs and translations. Every complete receipt must equal its frozen bytes. From the repository root:

```sh
python3 -I -B research/ordered-centre-interfaces/annexes/rank-completions/replay.py --out /tmp/ordered-rank-completions
```

Use Python 3.10 or later, a new output directory, one process, and at least 3 GiB free. The final line is:

```text
PASS_ORDERED_RANK_COMPLETIONS_ANNEX
```

The contraction uses 128 monomial wrappers, retains 128 real scalar primitives for its complex signs, and adds no owned or private field. Its native child moment falls for equal field volume and `0<sigma<1`, but the inherited normalized native moment remains above one for every positive saving exponent. Neither result gives a complete supplier or kappa improvement. Recursive child implementations, complete cover and map prices, finite precision, and revised recursive hosting were not rerun.

The [access/algebra annex](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/70b3c9ad0ee50502f91c31834ac7babc2ff52515/research/ordered-centre-interfaces/annexes/access-algebra/PROOF.md) adds the accepted future D73 bridge and ordered partner-retirement theorem. The bridge binds all 144 historical cuts, complete phases, owner paths, and arbitrary borrowed state. One update costs 4,992 real scalar primitives and 224 affine map applications, with no added native child or field. The array maps still need a finite price. The matched controller endpoint permits arbitrary W and T when the final X tail matches W. For idempotent P, later query preservation holds exactly when `P_i W_(i-1)=P_i T_(i-1)=0`; the first response remains separate. This proof covers every positive pair count.

The partner theorem cancels all 112 borrowed coefficients from physical Y and proves a unit retired code and a unit triangular X borrowed coefficient under the stated ordinary principal-unit hypotheses. It permits an arbitrary preceding selected data coefficient. Both actual ordinary blocks have 104 ports and determinant `2^60`; their separate 64-port component must be retained. This is local algebra, not admission of the partner-F16 native emission. The direct hole-endpoint route needs 208 native lines and eight even-line monomial maps. The 112-line route reaches FULL original data instead. Neither count is a universal decoder lower bound or a complete invoice.

The [source pins](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/70b3c9ad0ee50502f91c31834ac7babc2ff52515/research/ordered-centre-interfaces/annexes/access-algebra/SOURCES.json), [credit and license](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/70b3c9ad0ee50502f91c31834ac7babc2ff52515/research/ordered-centre-interfaces/annexes/access-algebra/NOTICE.md), and [separate review](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/70b3c9ad0ee50502f91c31834ac7babc2ff52515/research/publication-reviews/ordered-centre-interfaces/access-algebra-review/REVIEW.md) preserve the exact accepted sources. The replay runs all three unchanged independent checkers in normal and optimized Python and requires fresh receipts equal to the frozen bytes. It checks all 8,064 phase cases, the complete historical owner/helper ledger, ordered controller words, all local and original retirement columns, and both principal inverse orders. Negative controls reject missing or misordered translations, wrong tail coefficients, early reset, missing Q or the ordinary gauge, and illegal Q/graph commutation. From the repository root:

```sh
python3 -I -B research/ordered-centre-interfaces/annexes/access-algebra/replay.py --out /tmp/ordered-access-algebra
```

Use Python 3.10 or later, a new output directory, one process, and at least 3 GiB free. The final line is:

```text
PASS_ORDERED_ACCESS_ALGEBRA_ANNEX
```

New native words, physical inter-stage identifications, a global decoder, finite map prices, precision, and recursive hosting remain separate obligations. Producer dependency suites and native emitters were not rerun. This annex gives no complete supplier or kappa improvement.
